column3: on start, compare the native version with the bundled package.json version; when they differ, remember it in sessionStorage and reload the page with `?prism-version=` so WebView2 drops a cached old bundle
column5: Not ported. It exists only because WebView2 can serve a cached entry document after the native binary updates. The GPUI binary is the UI, so there is no separate bundle to go stale.

column3: on `prism-toggle` with open=false: hide("native"). With open=true: dismiss transient UI, reset the palette (no leftover query, selection, or settings), close settings, clear the close timer, reduce phase with "open"; when the result is Visible, present the window: not presented -> "present-failed"; presented -> focus the search input; a rejected present -> "present-failed"
column5: Root view handles `CoreEvent::Toggle(PalettePresentation { open, .. })` in the same order: close -> `hide(Native)`; open -> `TransientUi::dismiss_all`, `palette.reset()`, `app.set_open_settings(false)`, drop `close_task`, `phase = reduce(phase, Open)`; when Visible, spawn `backend.present_palette()`: Ok(false) or Err -> reduce PresentFailed; Ok(true) -> focus_search.

column3: on mount, ask isWindowVisible(); if the native window is already visible while React thinks it is hidden, enter "preparing" (or "visible" outside Tauri)
column5: Not ported. It repairs a race where the web page loads after the native window was shown (comment :181-183). In GPUI the root view is created together with its window, and the window's visibility is owned by prism-app, so the two states cannot diverge.

column3: while phase is "preparing": present the native window after the DOM is committed; on success wait one animation frame, then reduce "presented" and focus the search input; on failure reduce "present-failed"; a phase change cancels the pending steps
column5: When phase becomes Preparing, the root view renders the prepared frame, then spawns `backend.present_palette()` in `present_task` (replaced on each phase change, which cancels). Ok(true) -> `window.on_next_frame(|…| { phase = reduce(phase, Presented); focus_search })`; Ok(false) or Err -> reduce PresentFailed.

column3: focus items by index with wrap; open cancels a pending close timer, clears closing, opens, and focuses the item on the next animation frame; close(animate) snaps or animates for POPOVER_MOTION_MS, ignoring a close when already closed
column5: View fields `open`, `closing`, `close_task: Option<Task<()>>`, item FocusHandles. `open_menu(index)` drops `close_task`, sets open, focuses item `index mod len` on the next frame. `close_menu(animate)` returns when neither open nor closing; drops `close_task`; snap -> closed now; animate -> closing, then a POPOVER_MOTION_MS task closes it.

column2: outside press, palette close, settings open
column3: while open: a pointer press outside the menu root closes it with animation; prism:close and transient dismiss close it at once; opening settings closes it at once; unmount clears the close timer
column5: While open: `on_mouse_down_out` on the menu root -> close_menu(true); registered with TransientUi and the root's close broadcast -> close_menu(false); observe AppState.open_settings -> close_menu(false) when it becomes true. Dropping the view drops `close_task`.

column3: ignore while busy; perform the power action; on success close the menu and broadcast prism:close; on error toast "Could not {shut down|lock|sleep|restart…}" with the error text; clear busy
column5: `busy: Option<PowerAction>`; task runs `backend.perform_power_action(action)`; Ok -> open=false and `RootView::close_palette`; Err -> toast title `Could not shut down` for shutdown, else `Could not {action}`.

column3: ArrowDown/ArrowUp move with wrap from the focused item (focusItem uses modulo), Home/End, Escape closes with animation and returns focus to the trigger button
column5: Menu key context with the same keys; Escape -> close_menu(true) then focus the trigger's FocusHandle.
